page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c3d server family. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor, featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded decompression tasks fall into the bottom 25%. Memory subsystem performance is a notable constraint, with memory bandwidth and PassMark memory scores ranking in the bottom 10% to 25% categories. Cryptographic execution, such as PassMark CPU encryption, and single-threaded compression tasks perform at average levels.

The c3d-highcpu-4 offers a compute-focused hardware profile with a low memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but have minimal memory footprints. Due to the weak multi-core scaling and limited memory bandwidth, it is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale software compilation, or complex multi-threaded processing. Appropriate workloads include lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, and small-scale text or cryptographic processing.
